A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Markovian CoT research, with matching formalism and retained arithmetic plots. Their complete text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original arithmetic and GSM8K experiments, CoT perturbation tests, cross-model evaluations, and generated examples.

after.justification: V4 reports original arithmetic, GSM8K, and Wikipedia experiments, including perturbation analyses, cross-model evaluations, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The Markovian text bottleneck, informativeness objective, and TEI/PG/PPO algorithms remain. V4 adds KL regularization and adapts GSM8K training from PPO to thresholded policy gradient, also using this approach for Wikipedia. These are limited training-procedure adaptations.

E1.justification: V4 retains fifteen-term addition and GSM8K but adds Wikipedia continuation prediction (Section 5.3). Predicting article text through a shorter intermediate state substantially extends the evaluated coverage beyond mathematical question answering.

E2.justification: The evaluated EI/PG/PPO comparator set in Figure 2 remains unchanged. V4 adds an explicit no-context pretrained-Llama reference in the Wikipedia experiment, reporting 16.9% accuracy. Appendix E's proposed formal-language and question-plus-CoT alternatives are discussed, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: GSM8K changes from Mistral 7B/PPO with 80 CoT tokens to Llama 3.1 8B/thresholded PG with 150 tokens and KL regularization. Reported LoRA alpha changes from 1 to 16, and prompts are revised. Wikipedia introduces a 200-input/50-CoT/100-prediction-token protocol and a baseline-adjusted perturbation measure. These reported revisions do not establish that the retained arithmetic experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V4 adds Wikipedia perturbation-severity sweeps and a continuation case study. GSM8K and Wikipedia transfer analyses with several reader models replace v3's arithmetic Mistral-to-Llama-2 analysis. Arithmetic perturbation curves and generated examples are retained, while v3 Appendix B's qualitative temperature, entropy, and beam-search failure observations are removed.

E5.justification: V3 gives one GSM8K accuracy pair marked n=1; v4 explicitly reports three training runs and their separate final accuracies. V4 also specifies four Wikipedia learning-curve runs and six runs for Figure 8. Existing four-run arithmetic aggregation remains, and neither version supplies confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3's GSM8K results of 24.64% to 35.71% are replaced by Llama results of 35.94% to 69.14%, with other runs reaching 58.23% and 62.85%. These use different settings and are not matched performance gains over v3. V4 adds Wikipedia results of 8.2% to 10.5%, below the 16.9% no-context reference, plus new transfer and perturbation findings. Arithmetic benchmark curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Figure 7 introduces a mathematical definition subtracting the untrained CoT's perturbation effect from the trained CoT's effect, and derives its reduction to informativeness under constant perturbations. The main Markovian definitions and policy-gradient derivation remain unchanged; Appendix E's Equation 9 repeats the existing objective.

C1.justification: The headline GSM8K contribution changes from an approximately 11-point Mistral gain to a 33.2-point Llama gain under different training. More substantially, the introduction changes completeness and maximal fragility from properties the approach 'aims to achieve' into properties it 'ensures.' Cross-model transfer was already a contribution in v3.

C2.justification: V4 adds explanations of Wikipedia's prompting-related performance deficit and the case study's selective copying and token-boundary alignment. It expands model-relative interpretability arguments and discusses baseline limitations in Appendix E. V3's specific opaque-compression warning and proposed training mitigations in the steganography appendix are removed, although the general question of interpretability for different audiences remains.

D1.justification: V4 supplies new task-specific prompts, Wikipedia token budgets, KL and sampling settings, an advantage-baseline decay factor, and revised script instructions. However, it removes v3 Appendix B's learning rate, 8-bit AdamW identification, arithmetic token limits, and temperature disclosure. Section 8 also drops the explicit repository URL. These additions and omissions materially revise the available reproduction information.

R1.justification: Section 2's related-work comparisons remain unchanged. V4 adds references for Llama 3, Phi-3, GPT-2, and Wikipedia and removes the Llama-2 report. Appendix E adds focused positioning around baseline suitability, including a new claim that alternative faithfulness definitions are insufficiently specified as training objectives.

P1.justification: V4 revises the abstract, contribution statements, and reproducibility prose; separates GSM8K from addition; moves stability guidance from Section 4.3 to Appendix A; reorganizes appendices; and removes acknowledgments. The main section sequence and most related-work, formalism, and algorithm prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 replaces the appendix GSM8K chart with a two-panel, three-run main-text figure and replaces the original transfer plot with a multi-reader display. It adds Wikipedia learning, four-panel perturbation, and transfer figures, and compacts the arithmetic examples. Retained plots are moved or resized, and Figure 2's caption is corrected. Some new captions conflict with their plots, notably Figure 8's producer/evaluator roles.

improvement.justification: V4 modestly strengthens the empirical case through three GSM8K runs, more reader models, and Wikipedia analyses that expose both useful behavior and weak absolute performance. These gains are partly offset by removed training/access details, inconsistent figure captions, and the unsupported strengthening of completeness and maximal-fragility claims. The higher GSM8K scores use different models and settings, so they do not themselves establish an improvement over v3's method.
